title: AI Medical Interpretation for Pharmacy Counseling
summary: Build a safer pharmacy counseling workflow with AI interpretation, teach-back, written translation, privacy checks, and clear escalation.
body_markdown:
###


In a United States pharmacy, an AI medical interpreter supports a live, two-way spoken conversation between a pharmacist and a patient who uses another language. It interprets questions and counseling in real time, while the pharmacist remains responsible for the medication decision, counseling, teach-back, and documentation.


###


In a United States dispensing encounter, verify the medicine, strength, dose, route, timing, duration, food instructions, important precautions, missed-dose steps, storage, and follow-up. AHRQ teach-back guidance, reviewed in May 2023, recommends asking the patient or caregiver to explain the plan in their own words so the care team can correct misunderstandings.


###


No. Interpretation supports a live spoken or signed exchange, while translation converts written content such as a label, Medication Guide, or after-visit instruction into another language. Pharmacy teams should coordinate both so spoken counseling and written directions use the same dose, units, timing, and precautions.


###


In the United States, HIPAA covered entities should review whether the vendor will handle protected health information, execute a Business Associate Agreement when applicable, and provide appropriate access, retention, audit, and security controls. Those controls support a compliant workflow, but a tool alone does not guarantee compliance.


###


A pharmacy should use or switch to a qualified human interpreter when the patient prefers one, audio quality prevents a reliable exchange, uncertainty remains after clarification and teach-back, the technology fails, or organizational policy calls for escalation. The choice should reflect the patient, medication, setting, and pharmacy policy.
